description: Given the head of a sorted linked list, delete all nodes that have duplicate numbers, leaving only distinct numbers from the original list. Return the linked list sorted as well.
intuition: Use a pointer that looks ahead to detect runs of duplicate values. When you find a value that repeats, skip the entire run. A dummy node before the head handles the case where the head itself has duplicates.
approach: Use a dummy node before head. For each node, check if it has duplicates (next node has same value). If so, skip all nodes with that value. If not, advance the pointer.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: head = [1,2,3,3,4,4,5]

dummy -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 3 -> 4 -> 4 -> 5
prev=dummy, head=1

head=1: next=2, 1!==2 -> no dup -> prev=node(1), head=2
head=2: next=3, 2!==3 -> no dup -> prev=node(2), head=3
head=3: next=3, 3===3 -> has dup!
  inner loop: head.next=3 and 3===3 -> head=node(3)
  head.next now points to node(4)
  prev.next = head.next = node(4) -> skip both 3s
  head = head.next = node(4)
head=4: next=4, 4===4 -> has dup!
  skip both 4s; prev.next = node(5)
  head = node(5)
head=5: next=null -> no dup -> prev=node(5), head=null

Return dummy.next = [1,2,5]
explanation:
1. Create a dummy node pointing to head.
2. prev tracks the last confirmed unique node.
3. If head has duplicates (head.val == head.next.val), skip all nodes with that value.
4. Set prev.next to skip over all duplicates.
5. If no duplicate, advance prev normally.
hints: A dummy node simplifies handling duplicates at the head of the list.
When you find a duplicate value, skip all nodes with that value.
Keep a prev pointer to rewire around duplicate groups.
